plan.english: It rained. Then the gods arrived together, and the Father was sitting above. Then Mother Earth stood up and called on Sky: "Father, hear me! And you, dear gods, listen to me. Heavy to me are the men, the cattle and the sheep. My heart is heavy, and I have grown tired. Who shall lift these men from me?" Then he spoke to her: "Mother, I have heard your word. Old men will die, and they will lie down in the earth. Then you will not be heavy. May the gods give you rest." Then they heard his word and became joyful. Then she sat down in peace. Death comes to old men, and she protects them. In the spring men give her a gift.

A cloud was creeping above. Then Sky called the gods together, and they came. Then the Sun stood up and called on the Father and the gods: "Sky, Father and gods, listen to me! When the cloud is hiding me, the people give me no gifts, and they do not see me." Then he heard it and said to the Wind: "Wind, blow! Drive the cloud away from the Sun!" Then the Wind said: "Father, I shall blow." Then he blew, and the cloud vanished. Then the Sun shone out, and the men gave gifts and made a hymn. The cloud creeps above, and the Wind drives it away.

title: Fire and Water before the gods

plan.english: It was getting dark. The gods arrived, and the Father seated them. Then Fire stood up and cried out: "Sky, Father, listen to me! When I burn on the hearth, Water comes and kills me." Then Water answered: "I do not seek you. You yourself seek me." Then he spoke: "Fire, sit down on the hearth! And you, Water, go to the rivers! And do not come to the hearth!" Then Fire sat down on the hearth, and Water went to the rivers. Fire lives on the hearth, and Water lives in the rivers. The fire warms the people, and the water gives the people to drink.

The gods were sitting together, and the Father asked: "Who will speak?" Then Dawn said: "Father, I come to men, and I bring them light. When I come, the men are lying down, and no one gives me a gift." Then he said: "Dawn, my daughter, I have heard you. Let the men give Dawn a hymn, and when she comes, let them stand up." Then the gods became joyful, and Dawn shone out. Dawn goes in front, and the Sun follows her.

The thunder was rumbling. The gods were coming together to Sky. Then Perkwunos thundered and cried out: "Listen, gods! I slew the serpent, and I freed the waters, and the men are alive. Where is my reward? No one gives me cattle." Then the Mother said: "I saw Perkwunos slaying it." Then the Father spoke: "Perkwunos, you slew the serpent. The men will give you bulls and a hymn. May the gods give you imperishable fame." Then Perkwunos thundered, and they became joyful. The men give bulls to him, and his name is famous.

The goddess of the river came to Sky and called on him: "Sky, Father, hear me! Filth is in my water, and my fish have died." Then he asked: "Who has thrown filth into your water?" Then she said: "The men have thrown it. What shall I do?" Then Perkwunos was saying: "Gods, kill these men!" Then the Mother said: "Do not kill them!" Then the Father said: "Listen to my word, gods! Whoever throws filth into the river, may he be thirsty, and may he not drink the water." Then she became joyful, and her water became washed. The fish swim in her water.

title: The Moon, the wolf and the dog

plan.english: It was getting dark, and the gods were sitting down together. The Moon spoke to the Father: "Father, the wolf comes in the night and devours the shepherd's sheep. The shepherd says: 'The Moon is dear to the wolf.' I am not dear to the wolf! I have seen the wolf." Then he asked: "Who guards the sheep?" Then she said: "The shepherd guards them." Then the Father said: "Shepherd, lead the dog to them! And let the dog guard them. When the wolf comes, let the dog cry out." Then the wolf fled, and the Moon shone. The shepherd made a hymn for the Moon, and the dog was sitting at the door.

The gods were speaking together: "Who of us is great?" Then Perkwunos said: "I slew the serpent, and I am great." Then Fire cried out: "I eat the gifts of the people, and I carry them to you." Then the gods looked at the Father. Then he said: "Great is the giver. I am the giver of good things." Then they heard it, and no one said a word. Then he raised his eyebrows.

title: The Mother and her two sons

plan.english: The two sons were standing opposite each other. Then the Mother led them to the Father and spoke: "Father, my two sons are standing opposite each other. Their words are heavy. I am their mother, and I do not know." Then he asked: "Who ploughed the field?" Then this one said: "I ploughed it with the plough." Then that one said: "My livestock is in the field." Then the Father said: "Hear me, you two! Let this one plough it, and let that one lead his own cattle to it." They heard his word, and they became joyful. She looked at them, and there was delight in her heart.

title: A name for the son of Sky

plan.english: The gods were going to the Father, and the son of Sky stood up and called on the Father: "Sky, Father, I have no name. Set a name for me!" Then Dawn said: "May his name be swift." Then the Father said: "He is my son, and men will hear his name." Then he set a famous name on him, and the gods became joyful. His name is famous, and his fame is imperishable.

It dawned, and Perkwunos and Fire were driving many cattle. Perkwunos was saying: "These cattle are mine. My hand drove them. I shall strike you." Then Fire was saying: "You are deceiving me. My mouth called them. I led the cattle out. I shall burn you." Then Dawn came between them and spoke: "Do not strike him, Perkwunos! Do not burn him, Fire! Let us go to Sky, and let us ask him." Then they arrived at him, and he said: "These cattle are Dawn's." Then Dawn drove her own cattle away. The two of them became afraid.

The Wind and the Sun were sitting together. A man wearing a garment was walking on the narrow path. The Wind said: "I am swift, and I drive the clouds." Then it said: "I am great, and I warm men. Who has power? Wind, blow! If the man lets go of his garment, you have won." The Wind blew thrice, but that one held his own garment. Then the man trembled. Then it heated him, and that one was sweating, and he let go of the garment. Then the Sun won.

Sky gave swift horses to Dawn. Then the Wind came to him and said: "Sky, Father, you gave swift horses to Dawn, and you gave me nothing." Then the Father asked: "What do you carry?" The Wind said: "I carry the clouds and the breath of men." Then the Father said: "I have heard your word. Let the clouds be your swift horses, and harness them!" Then the Wind harnessed the clouds and drove them on. Dawn and the Wind went together, and the men saw them. The clouds ran, and the thunder rumbled.

The serpent was crawling in the marsh and spoke: "No one has overpowered me. I have enclosed the waters, and I am great. My teeth are many." The rivers were not flowing, and the men were thirsty. The tears of the men fell. Perkwunos was listening well. He heard its word, and he stood up, and he seized bronze, and he came. Then Perkwunos said: "Might is mine. I shall slay you." Then the serpent seized Perkwunos. Perkwunos thundered, and he slew the serpent with bronze. Then the waters became free. They set great fame on him, and men listen to his famous name. He is the slayer of the serpent, and they make a hymn for him. Great is his stature.

title: Sky and Earth ask each other

plan.english: Sky and the Mother were sitting together. "Who of us knows?" Then he asked: "What is born from me and comes to you?" Then she answered: "Water is born from you, and it comes to me." Then she asked: "What lies in the earth and grows up to you?" Then he answered: "Grain lies in the earth, and it grows up to me." Then Dawn said: "Sky knows the water, and the Mother knows the grain. Her knowledge is great." Then the two of them became joyful.

title: Dawn lifts the wheel of the sun

plan.english: The wheel of the sun lay in the field. Then the Father said: "Gods, whoever lifts the wheel, to him I shall give a gift. Who has power?" Then Perkwunos lifted the wheel, but he did not have power. Then Fire seized it, but the wheel was heavy. Then Dawn stood up, and she lifted the wheel and carried it up. Then the Father said: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, you have lifted the wheel. I shall give you a good gift." Dawn carries it up, and men see her.

title: Night and Dawn on the path

plan.english: Night and Dawn are two sisters. It was getting dark. Night was standing on the narrow path, and Dawn was coming. Then Night said: "Sister, this path is mine, and I give the men rest." Then Dawn said: "Sister, do not stand on the path! Go away! The men look at me, and my tears sink into the field." Then the Mother said: "You two are my daughters. Night, go in front! And you, Dawn, follow her." Then Night went down, and Dawn shone out. Night goes in front, and Dawn follows her.

Sky and Earth were sitting together. "Who gives the men grain?" Then he said: "I give water to this earth. If there is no water, the grain dies." Then the Mother said: "I protect the grain, and I nourish it, and I lift it to you. If I do not nourish it, what are you giving?" Then Dawn said: "From that heaven comes water, and from this earth comes grain. Together you give the men grain." The men eat it. Then the two of them became joyful.

The Sun came to Sky and called on him: "Father, give me your daughter! I shall give you a hundred cattle." Then he said: "Her bride price is a thousand cattle." Then the Sun was saying: "I do not have a thousand cattle. I shall give you seven swift horses." Then he said: "Good is the price. I shall give you my daughter." Then Dawn sat down on the wagon of the Sun, and it led her away. The seven swift horses carried the wagon. The people made a hymn, and a hundred cattle followed.

title: The race of the Wind and Fire

plan.english: The gods were sitting. Then the Father said: "Wind and Fire, run against each other! Who will win?" Then the Wind went in front, and Fire cried out: "Wind, blow at me!" Then he blew, and Fire ran through the field and burned it. The field was red. Then Fire won. They were looking on. Then the Mother said: "If the Wind does not blow, Fire does not go. Father, give a prize to the Wind and to Fire!" Then he gave a prize to them.

title: The cattle of Sky and the old man

plan.english: A swift god stole the cattle of Sky in the night and drove them to the field. Then he drove them to the river, and the cattle were swimming. Then he hid them in the marsh. An old man was sitting at the door. The old man was listening well. He saw the god and recognized him. At dawn Sky looked at his own cattle and did not see them. Then he called the old man: "Who has taken my cattle?" Then the old man said: "The god took them. I saw him." Then the Father was saying: "Swift god, you stole my cattle. Lead them back!" Then the swift god became afraid and led the cattle back, and he gave two bulls. "Father, do not strike me!" Then the Father said: "Live! And do not steal again."

title: Fire from the hearth of the gods

plan.english: The swift god came to the hearth of the gods. The fire was burning on the hearth, and its light was great. He stole the fire from the hearth and carried it down to men. Then Sky called him: "Did you steal the fire from my hearth?" Then the swift god spoke: "I stole the fire. The men became cold. Then I carried the fire to them, and they became warm." Then the Father said: "The fire is a gift to men. But give the gods a hymn!" Then the god gave the gods a hymn, and they became joyful. People guard the fire on their own hearths, and the fire warms them.

The Mother had many sheep. Now the sheep are gone. Then the Mother tracked the path, and on the path she saw the hoofs of the sheep. She came to the river. The river was deep. At the river a god was sitting, and he was carrying washed wool. Then she asked: "Who are you? Whose is this wool?" Then the god said: "The wool is mine." She said: "You are deceiving me." Then she called her own sheep. They heard and ran to her. Then the god became afraid. "Mother, I took them. Do not strike me!" Then she spoke: "Bring me the wool and a gift!" Then the god brought the Mother wool and a gift, and she led her own sheep home.

A shepherd was guarding the livestock of Sky, and the dog was with him. The dog was alert. The shepherd lay down. Then a god came to the field. He stole the shepherd's garment and put it on. The dog saw the garment and licked the god. Then the god drove the livestock away. The shepherd woke up. "Where is the livestock? Dog, you licked a stranger!" Then the Father found him on the path and seized him. Then the god led the livestock back, and he gave the garment to the shepherd. Since then the dog cries out at a stranger.

The cattle of Sky were in the earth, and a serpent guarded the door. The god came to the door and cried out: "Serpent, I am your friend. I bring you many sheep." Then the serpent cried out: "Come in!" Then the god went in, and the serpent devoured them. And he became sated, and he lay down. Then the god drove the cattle out. He had deceived the serpent. The serpent woke up and said: "Where are the cattle?" Then Sky gave the god good fame.

Two gods made a pledge. "This one shall give cattle, and that one a horse." This one gave the cattle, and that one took them. Then this one cried out: "Where is my horse?" Then that one said: "I did not take your cattle. Sky knows my pledge. If I am deceiving you, may Sky strike me." Then Sky heard him and thundered. Then that one became afraid and gave the horse to this one. Sky is the knower of a pledge.

title: The song of the son of the Moon

plan.english: In the night the son of the Moon stole the cattle of Sky and drove them away. Then Sky seized him and asked: "Did you steal my cattle?" Then the god was saying: "I did not see the cattle." Then the Father said: "You have deceived me. Your hand drove them." Then the god made a good song, and the Father listened. There was delight in his heart, and he spoke: "Son of the Moon, I have heard your song. Lead my cattle back to me, and I shall give you two bulls." Then the god led them back.

title: The Mother awake at her door

plan.english: It was getting dark. The Mother lay down at her own door. A swift god saw her and said: "She is lying down. She does not see me. I shall drive away her cattle." Then he drove away her cattle. Then she seized his hand and said: "I was awake. I was looking at you. I know you." Then the god became afraid. "Mother, I shall guard your cattle." Then she spoke: "Guard them! And lead them to the field. I shall give you livestock. The Mother is knowing." Then the god guarded her cattle in the night.

A man was ploughing the field with a plough. He grew tired and sat down. Then the Mother appeared to him and spoke: "Man, with a plough you plough me. I nourish you and your cattle. If you give me a gift, I shall give you grain." Then the man asked: "What shall I give you?" Then she answered: "Give me seed." Then the man put the seed in the earth, and she gave him much grain. The grain grew. Then the man made a hymn for her.

title: The king who gave no gifts

plan.english: A king was being carried in a ship on the deep lake, and he was saying: "I am the king of men. I am great. I give no gift to the gods." An old man in the ship said: "King, do not speak so! Sky is listening to you." The king did not hear the old man. Then Sky heard the king, thundered and spoke: "King, you have spoken a heavy word. Whoever gives no gift to the gods, his ship shall sink." Then the wind blew, and the lake was agitated. Then the ship sank, and the king died. And men did not call on his name.

title: The guest at the old man's door

plan.english: An old man and his wife lived on the path. His wife was cooking the grain. It rained, and in the night a guest came. The old man said: "Guest, sit down! Eat the cooked grain! Drink the water! I have a lamb. I shall kill it." Then the guest said: "Do not kill the lamb! I am not a stranger. I am a god. Old man, you gave me cooked grain and water. I shall give you much livestock and good fame. May your lifetime grow." Then the guest vanished. Then the old man saw livestock in the field, and his wife became joyful.

title: Sky and the killer of the guest

plan.english: A man killed a guest and seized his cattle. Sky saw it. Then he asked the man: "Where is the guest?" Then the man answered: "I do not know." Then the Father said: "You know. You are deceiving me. A guest comes from Sky. Your cattle will die, and you will lie in the earth. Death will come to you." Then he thundered, and the man died. Men protect the guest.

A wife was walking on the path and crying out. Her husband had died, and her tears fell. It dawned, and Dawn came forth to her. The wife looked at her and called on her: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, hear me! My husband has died. What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Wife, do not cry out! I have heard you. Death comes to men, but fame does not die. I shall give you a son. He will be of good fame, and his might will be great." Then the wife asked: "What shall I give you?" Then Dawn said: "Give me a hymn." Then the wife made a hymn for Dawn and gave her a gift. Then Dawn vanished. In the year a son came to her. His name was famous.

The path was narrow, and it was getting dark. A man was walking in the night. He did not see it, and he became afraid. A wolf cried out. Then the Moon shone and showed the man the path. Then the man cried out: "Who are you?" Then she said: "I am the Moon. I am Dawn's sister. I walk in the night. My light is on the path. Do not tremble! Follow me!" Then the man asked: "Where is the settlement?" Then she said: "The settlement is yonder." Then the man followed her and arrived at the settlement. Then the man gave the Moon an offering, and he became joyful.

It dawned. Dawn, the daughter of Sky, stood up and was saying to the people. "Wake up, people! I am coming, and I am red, and I bring you light. Shepherd, stand up and lead the sheep to it! Man, wake up and yoke the cattle with the yoke! Wife, rise, milk the cattle, heat the water and cook the grain! Sons and daughters, do not lie down! Old man, sit at the door and look at the path. If you do not rise, the Sun will see you lying down. Who has risen? To him I shall give good fame. Give me a hymn, and I shall give you good things." Then the people woke up, and the Sun shone out. The shepherd led the sheep, the man yoked the cattle, and the wife milked them.

Mother Earth was saying to her own sons and daughters: "Listen, sons and daughters! I nourish you, and I protect you. From me comes grain. From me comes the well. From me comes the water. Cold comes, and snow comes. In the spring the grain stands up from me. If you give me a gift, I shall give you grain. Do not split me! Your fathers lie in the earth, and you will lie in the earth." Then the people heard the Mother.

title: The Mother speaks to the gods

plan.english: The Mother called her own sons, and they came to her. Then she was saying: "Hear me, my sons! I am your mother, and Sky is your father. You sit above, and I lie below. Whoever strikes his own brother strikes me. My heart is heavy. Do not strike! Sit together, eat and drink together. A brother is a friend." Then they heard their own mother and sat down. She looked at them, and there was delight in her heart.

Dawn was saying to the Sun: "Sun, come! Harness your swift horses! I go in front, and you follow me. Give light to the people! Warm the livestock! Dry my tears!" Then it answered: "Dawn, daughter of Sky, I am listening to you. Where shall I go? What shall I do?" Then Dawn said: "Go up! Look at the settlement and the path. The men are lying down." Then it harnessed the horses and went up. Then it shone, and Dawn vanished. Her tears dried up.

Earth called on Sky: "Sky, my husband, hear me! I am thirsty, and the field has dried up. The rivers do not flow. My sheep are thirsty, and my cattle lie down. My heart is heavy. Drive the clouds! Give thunder! Let it rain! If it rains, the grain will grow, and the sheep will drink. I shall give you grain and a hymn." Then he said: "My wife, I have heard your word. Last year you gave me no gift." Then she answered: "Last year it did not rain. If it rains, I shall give you a gift." Then he said: "I shall drive the clouds, and the thunder will roar." Then it rained, and the rivers became full. The grain grew in it, and they drank. She made a hymn for him.

title: The Mother at the turning of the year

plan.english: The Mother was saying to the people: "My sons and daughters, listen! Spring is coming, and the snow is melting. The rivers are swelling. Throw the seed into the field! Drive the cattle to it! Protect the sheep, and milk the cattle! Remember your fathers and the gods. If you give gifts to the gods, they will give you cattle and sheep. Do not sit down: work!" Then a man cried out: "Mother, what shall we throw into the field?" Then she answered: "Throw the seed, the grain. Throw it into the field." Then the people heard the Mother, and they went to it. In the spring the people were working. She looked at them, and there was delight in her heart.
